records.title: The Stanford CoreNLP Natural Language Processing Toolkit
records.reason: The primary paper describes an extensible pipeline for core natural-language analysis, including tokenization, tagging, parsing, and coreference. It is a general NLP toolkit paper and presents no LLM inference/serving system or inference-time compression/efficiency contribution. A toolkit or neural NLP component alone is outside the stated scope.
records.body_check: Primary ACL Anthology metadata and PDF abstract checked. The abstract characterizes CoreNLP as an extensible pipeline for core natural-language analysis; the introduction enumerates standard analysis components. The paper is about toolkit design and use, not LLM inference or efficiency. Abstract-level evidence is sufficient for this clear exclusion; full text was not reviewed.

records.title: Word Association Norms, Mutual Information, and Lexicography
records.reason: The primary abstract proposes mutual-information-based estimates of word association norms from corpora, with applications in lexicography and other language-processing tasks. Although one listed application is constraining language models for speech recognition/OCR, the contribution is a corpus-derived lexical statistic, not an LLM inference/serving technique or an inference-efficiency method. Mentioning a language-model application does not make it in scope.
records.body_check: Primary ACL Anthology record and PDF abstract checked. The DOI in the brief resolves via the Anthology record to P89-1010, with matching title and authors; the supplied 981623.981633-style Anthology URL was not the current canonical path. The abstract defines an information-theoretic measure to estimate word-association norms from text corpora and lists applications including language-model constraints for speech recognition/OCR, parsing, retrieval, and lexicography. No LLM inference, serving, or efficiency contribution is claimed. Abstract-only evidence is sufficient for this clear exclusion; full text was not reviewed.

records.title: Hierarchical Attention Networks for Document Classification
records.reason: The primary abstract describes a hierarchical neural architecture with word- and sentence-level attention for document classification, evaluated on six text-classification tasks. It reports task-performance improvements, not an LLM inference/serving system or inference-time efficiency/compression contribution. A general neural NLP architecture alone is outside the stated scope.
records.body_check: Primary ACL Anthology metadata and PDF abstract checked. The abstract and introduction identify the contribution as a document-classification model with hierarchical structure and two attention levels, evaluated on six text-classification tasks. No inference/serving optimization is claimed. Abstract-only evidence is sufficient for this clear exclusion; full text was not reviewed.
